He played one season of college basketball for the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]]. ==Early life== Magnay was born in [[Brisbane]], [[Queensland]],{{cite web |title=Will Magnay Bio |url=https://tulsahurricane.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/will-magnay/5461 |website=Tulsa Hurricane |access-date=22 November 2019}} where he attended [[St Joseph's College, Nudgee|Nudgee College]].{{cite web |title=Player Profile: Will Magnay |url=http://www.brisbanebullets.com.au/news/article/player-profile-will-magnay |website=Brisbane Bullets |access-date=22 November 2019}} He played for the [[Northside Wizards]] as a junior. He moved to the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] in [[Canberra]], where he played for the [[BA Centre of Excellence]] in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]] in 2016.{{cite web |title=Will Magnay |url=https://websites.mygameday.app/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=199809460&client=1-3363-150604-402777-20161522 |website=SEABL |access-date=2 May 2022}} ==College career== Magnay played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]] during the 2016–17 season. He averaged 3.9 points and 3 rebounds in 32 games played.{{cite web |last1=Hines |first1=Kelly |title=TU center Will Magnay leaves team to turn pro in Australia |url=https://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/tusportsextra/tu-center-will-magnay-leaves-team-to-turn-pro-in/article_923f1436-41f0-56f2-8570-d7d27ab04195.html |website=Tulsa World |access-date=22 November 2019 |date=4 October 2017}} ==Professional career== ===NBL=== In October 2017, Magnay left the Tulsa Golden Hurricane program and signed a three-year deal with his hometown team, the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/BrisbaneBullets/status/915448163443470337|title=#BREAKING Magnay signs with the Bullets|website=twitter.com/BrisbaneBullets|date=4 October 2017|access-date=4 May 2021}} He spent the [[2017–18 NBL season]] as a development player. For the [[2018–19 NBL season]], Magnay was elevated to a fully-rostered player.{{cite web |title=Brisbane Bullets add fire-power to their future with Magnay signing |url=http://www.brisbanebullets.com.au/news/article/brisbane-bullets-add-fire-power-future-magnay-signing |website=Brisbane Bullets |access-date=22 November 2019}} Magnay had a breakout year during the [[2019–20 NBL season]] that saw him enter the Bullets' starting line-up and receive attention from [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) scouts.{{cite web |last1=Wenzel |first1=Murray |title=Magnay backed as Bullets eye NBL finals |url=https://www.katherinetimes.com.au/story/6618892/magnay-backed-as-bullets-eye-nbl-finals/ |website=Katherine Times |access-date=17 November 2020 |date=7 February 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Stannard |first1=Damien |title=Rival coach in awe of Bullet's shot-blocking power |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/rival-coach-in-awe-of-bullet-s-shot-blocking-power-20200124-p53uk4.html |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=17 November 2020 |date=24 January 2020}} He was subsequently named the [[NBL Most Improved Player Award|NBL Most Improved Player]] for the 2019–20 season{{cite news |last1=Gilhooly |first1=Daniel |title=NBL award winners announced |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/28714451/nbl-award-winners-announced |access-date=21 February 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=16 February 2020}} and initially re-signed with the Bullets on a two-year contract.{{cite web |title=Will Magnay Re-Signs With Brisbane Bullets |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/will-magnay-re-signs-with-brisbane-bullets |website=NBL |access-date=17 November 2020 |date=19 February 2020 |archive-date=1 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301013119/https://nbl.com.au/news/will-magnay-re-signs-with-brisbane-bullets |url-status=dead }} On 6 May 2021, following an NBA stint, Magnay signed with the [[Perth Wildcats]] for the rest of the [[2020–21 NBL season]].{{cite web |title=Will Magnay Signs with Perth |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/will-magnay-signs-with-perth |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=6 May 2021 |date=6 May 2021}} He averaged 4.7 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game in 15 games played with the Wildcats.{{cite web |title=Magnay to move on |url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/magnay-to-move-on |website=Wildcats.com.au |access-date=3 July 2021 |date=3 July 2021}} On 12 July 2021, Magnay signed a one-year deal with the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]], a new club entering the NBL for the first time in [[2021–22 NBL season|2021–22]].{{cite web |title=Will Magnay Joins the JackJumpers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/will-magnay-joins-the-jackjumpers |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=12 July 2021 |date=12 July 2021}} He was limited to 11 games in 2021–22 due to a knee injury.{{cite web |title=Magnay Re-Signs with JackJumpers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/magnay-re-signs-with-jackjumpers |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=21 April 2022 |date=21 April 2022}} He subsequently re-signed with the JackJumpers on a two-year deal on 21 April 2022. Magnay missed the start of the [[2023–24 NBL season]] due to a foot injury.{{cite web |title=Magnay returns for JackJumpers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/magnay-returns-for-jackjumpers |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=10 November 2023 |date=10 November 2023}} He went on to help the JackJumpers win their maiden [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] with a 3–2 grand final series victory over [[Melbourne United]],{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/tasmania-jackjumpers-nbl24-champions|title=Tasmania JackJumpers: NBL24 Champions|work=NBL.com.au|date=31 March 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240331074750/https://nbl.com.au/news/tasmania-jackjumpers-nbl24-champions|archive-date=31 March 2024}} On 10 March 2024, Magnay re-signed with the JackJumpers on a two-year deal.{{cite web|title=Magnay-ficent: JackJumpers secure key signature|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/magnay-ficent-jackjumpers-secure-key-signature|website=NBL.com.au|access-date=10 March 2024|date=10 March 2024}} On 19 December 2024, he was ruled out for six to eight weeks after suffering a fractured toe in practice.{{cite news |title=Magnay out 6-8 weeks |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/magnay-out-6-8-weeks |access-date=19 December 2024 |work=NBL Official Website |date=19 December 2024}} Magnay was named JackJumpers captain for the [[2025–26 NBL season]].{{cite news |title=Magnay and Drmic to lead playing group in NBL26 |url=https://www.jackjumpers.com.au/news/magnay-and-drmic-to-lead-playing-group-in-nbl26 |access-date=4 September 2025 |work=Tasmania JackJumpers {{!}} Official NBL Website |date=4 September 2025}} On 12 November 2025, he was sidelined due to a knee injury.{{cite news |title=Injury sidelines JackJumpers star |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/injury-sidelines-jackjumper-star-will-magnay |access-date=12 November 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=12 November 2025 |language=en}} On 21 January 2026, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with an acute fracture of the second toe on his left foot.{{cite news |title=JackJumpers star ruled out for season |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/tasmania-jackjumpers-star-will-magnay-ruled-out-for-season |access-date=21 January 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=21 January 2026 |language=en}} Over his first five seasons for the JackJumpers, he played just 56 per cent all of games.{{cite news |title=Contract calls loom on JackJumpers stars |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/scott-roth-jackjumpers-offseason-decisions |access-date=13 March 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=13 March 2026 |language=en}} On 12 May 2026, Magnay re-signed with the JackJumpers on a two-year deal.{{cite news |title=BREAKING: JackJumpers captain re-signs on multi-year deal |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/jackjumpers-capitan-will-magnay-re-signs-on-multi-year-deal |access-date=12 May 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=12 May 2026 |language=en}} ===NBA=== On 2 December 2020, Magnay signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]].{{cite web |title=Pelicans sign four players |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-four-players |website=NBA.com |access-date=3 December 2020 |date=2 December 2020}} He played 10 games for the BayHawks in February 2021 during the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|G League hub season]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/player/will-magnay/|title=Will Magnay|work=gleague.nba.com|accessdate=4 May 2021}} He made his NBA debut on 23 March 2021 against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], going scoreless over the final three minutes of the game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=401307452|title=Ingram, Williamson pace Pelicans in 128-111 win over Lakers|work=ESPN.com|date=23 March 2021|accessdate=4 May 2021|quote=Australian rookie Will Magnay saw his first NBA action in the final three minutes. He attempted one shot from 3-point range and missed.}} On 12 April 2021, he was waived by the Pelicans.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign James Nunnally to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-james-nunnally-two-way-contract|date=12 April 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=12 April 2021}} In July 2025, Magnay joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news |title=Magnay delivers in first Vegas test |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/magnay-delivers-in-first-vegas-test |access-date=18 July 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=16 July 2025 |language=en}}{{cite news |title=Revealed: Why Magnay almost walked away from basketball |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/revealed-why-magnay-almost-walked-away-from-basketball |access-date=18 July 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=18 July 2025 |language=en}} ===Europe=== In February 2023, Magnay joined Spanish club [[Obradoiro CAB]] of the [[Liga ACB]] for the rest of the 2022–23 season.{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/will-magnay-joins-obradoiro/|title=Will Magnay joins Obradoiro|work=sportando.basketball|date=February 21, 2023|access-date=February 22, 2023 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} On 9 March 2025, Magnay signed with [[Mersin MSK]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) for the rest of the 2024–25 season.{{Cite tweet |user=mersin_msk |number=1898754250760421826 |title=Takımımız, bu sezon Tasmania JackJumpers forması giyen tecrübeli pivot oyuncusu Will Scott Magnay ile anlaşmıştır.}} ===State leagues=== Magnay played for the Southern Districts Spartans of the [[Queensland Basketball League]] (QBL) during the 2018 season.{{Cite web|url=https://qbl.basketballqld.com.au/2018-qbl-pre-season-write-up/|title=2018 QBL PRE-SEASON WRITE-UP|website=qbl.basketballqld.com.au|date=24 April 2018|access-date=4 May 2021|quote=Bullets big man Will Magnay is a player to keep an eye on.}} In [[2019 Queensland Basketball League season|2019]], he helped the [[Brisbane Capitals]] win the [[List of NBL1 North champions|QBL championship]].{{cite web|last=Kay|first=Oliver|url=https://pickandroll.com.au/p/meet-will-magnay-brisbane-bullets-emerging-sky-walker|title=Meet Will Magnay: The Brisbane Bullets' emerging sky walker|work=pickandroll.com.au|date=27 September 2019|access-date=4 May 2021}} Magnay joined the [[Gold Coast Rollers (NBL1 North)|Gold Coast Rollers]] of the [[NBL1 North]] for the [[2024 NBL1 season|2024 season]].{{cite web|title=2024 GOLD COAST BASKETBALL NBL1 NORTH PLAYER ANNOUNCEMENT.|url=https://www.facebook.com/GoldCoastBasketballPage/posts/pfbid0ZafBtFWdbV1Xoy43VbmZ6spXYv2vfR3i3Ni7FPMCxa3Ls1sjagFFFboHMBhWXy8Pl|website=facebook.com/GoldCoastBasketballPage|access-date=17 March 2024|date=16 March 2024}}{{cite web|title=NBL superstar joins Gold Coast|url=https://nbl1.com.au/news/nbl-superstar-joins-gold-coast|website=NBL1.com.au|access-date=17 March 2024|date=16 March 2024}} He appeared in four games for the Rollers.{{cite web |title=Will Magnay |url=https://goldcoastrollers.nbl1.com.au/player/3c15c86c-8f7f-11ee-bfc8-479efcbf0c3d/67a2bf87-0e9b-11ef-81f5-c5cefb9ff587/will-magnay |website=nbl1.com.au |access-date=24 March 2025}} ==National team career== In July 2024, Magnay was named in the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian Boomers]]' final squad for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Paris Olympics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4052425/australian-teams-for-paris-2024-olympics-announced|title=Australian teams for Paris 2024 Olympics announced|work=[[Basketball Australia]]|date=6 July 2024|access-date=7 July 2024}} In July 2025, Magnay was named in the Boomers squad in the lead up to the [[2025 FIBA Asia Cup]] in Saudi Arabia.{{cite news |title=Balanced Boomers for University of Colorado |url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4300205/balanced-boomers-for-university-of-colorado |access-date=3 July 2025 |work=www.australia.basketball |date=3 July 2025 |language=en}}{{cite news |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=Generationally diverse extended Australian Boomers squad named |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/45650023/generationally-diverse-extended-australian-boomers-squad-named |access-date=3 July 2025 |work=ESPN.com |date=3 July 2025 |language=en}} He was named captain of the team for the tournament.{{cite news |title=Will's power: Magnay to lead Boomers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/magnay-to-captain-boomers |access-date=2 August 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=1 August 2025 |language=en}} In October 2025, Magnay was named in the Boomers squad for the first window of the [[2027 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers]].{{cite news |title=Boomers confirmed for NZ double-header |url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4388280/boomers-confirmed-for-nz-double-header |access-date=24 October 2025
